source_note: Locally curated MITRE ATT&CK technique summaries (paraphrased) for offline RAG. Not the full ATT&CK corpus.

items.title: Brute Force
items.summary: Adversaries repeatedly guess credentials, producing many failed authentications often followed by a success. Detect via failed-auth bursts per user/source and improbable success timing.

items.title: Remote Services: SSH
items.summary: Adversaries use valid credentials over SSH to move between hosts. Evidence: successful SSH auth from a new source host followed by process execution on the target.

items.title: Ingress Tool Transfer
items.summary: Adversaries transfer tools or payloads from an external system into the environment, often via curl/wget. Evidence: shell process spawning a download of a payload.

items.title: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
items.summary: Execution of commands via bash/sh. Evidence: process activity with shell command lines invoking network or file operations.

items.title: Valid Accounts
items.summary: Use of legitimate credentials to blend in. Evidence: authorised identity acting outside normal windows or on unassigned assets.

items.title: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
items.summary: Adversaries perform privileged actions (sudo, account creation). Evidence: privileged commands by a non-privileged or off-context identity.

items.title: Data from Local System
items.summary: Access to local data, including canary/decoy assets. Any interaction with a synthetic canary is high-signal in this cyber-range.
